claim: A human progressive-MS active-lesion CyTOF study reported higher CD44 together with HLA-DR, CD45, CD68 and other inflammatory or phagocytic markers in lesion-enriched activated microglial clusters relative to homeostatic microglia.
future_grounding_route: Use only as independent lesion-state context. An independent transcriptomic cohort with MS and control donors, normal-appearing tissue, CD44/CXCR4 coverage, and age/region metadata is still required for the frozen V53 replication test.
project_use: Independent human-tissue context for whether CD44 tracks a broad activated microglial state in MS lesions.
relationship_note: The source converges with the project's broad-state-bounded interpretation for CD44, but it studies active lesions and protein-marker clusters rather than the exact normal-appearing-tissue two-gene transcript score. It is context corroboration, not replication.

source.citation: Bottcher et al. Single-cell mass cytometry reveals complex myeloid cell composition in active lesions of progressive multiple sclerosis. Acta Neuropathologica Communications. 2020.
source.label: Bottcher 2020 progressive-MS active-lesion CyTOF study

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PubMed Central open article; metadata and short paraphrase reused
source_terms.reuse_notes: This record stores bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase only; no source data or article text is redistributed.

why_unverifiable: The project has not rerun the external study's CyTOF analysis or obtained its sample-level measurements.
